subject: Cross-border transfer evidence, runbook and safeguards — supplemental Q&A
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@globalhealthsys.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procure-ops@globalhealthsys.com
Date: 2028-06-10T09:14:00Z
Subject: Request for transfer evidence & runbook for DPF review

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the routing and fallback story. As part of our Risk & Compliance gate we need a short evidence pack to complete the DPF assessment. Specifically: 

- A one-page operational runbook showing how cross-border requests are routed and how regional pinning works (we'll need an on-prem option noted).
- The DPA annex draft with the sections covering subprocessors and international transfers.
- Any statements or supporting docs describing which transfer mechanisms you rely on (SCCs, EU DPF approvals, encryption-at-rest key handling).
- A high-level network map showing where data is processed and what controls apply (redact IPs if necessary).

Can you send a preliminary pack by EOD Tuesday? Our compliance reviewer (Anna Müller) will go through and come back with follow-ups.

Deal is referenced as DEAL-4832 on our side. Thanks — Liam

--
Liam O'Connor
Head of Procurement
GlobalHealth Systems
liam.oconnor@globalhealthsys.com
+44 20 7123 4455
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@globalhealthsys.com>
Cc: procure-ops@globalhealthsys.com
Date: 2028-06-11T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request for transfer evidence & runbook for DPF review

Hi Liam,

Appreciate the clear ask. Attaching an initial bundle that should cover the items you listed: redwood-transfer-runbook.pdf (operational runbook), dpa-annex-draft.docx (editable), scc-statements.pdf, and a redacted network-map.png. I've also included a short FAQ at the front of the runbook that highlights the private deployment options and regional pinning behavior.

High-level notes up front: 
- We operate under SCCs for EU→US transfers for hosted customers by default and support DPF-approved flows where customers require it.
- Customers on Redwood Private can restrict processing to a specific region; our VPC/on-prem package supports air-gapped deployments.
- Keys: we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; by default hosted keys are managed via our KMS with envelope encryption.

Anna — welcome; if you want a dedicated walkthrough of the runbook we can schedule 30 minutes next week.

Deliverables attached. Will loop legal and security internally for any requested changes to the DPA annex.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Attachment(s): redwood-transfer-runbook.pdf (18 pages), dpa-annex-draft.docx (editable), scc-statements.pdf (4 pages), network-map.png
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-12T09:37:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Request for transfer evidence & runbook for DPF review

Vanessa / Karthik — forwarding the request from GlobalHealth. I reviewed the dpa-annex-draft.docx and have a few comments inline:

- Section 3.2 (subprocessors): we need to list the specific cloud provider regions and subprocessors for audit purposes; propose adding a managed-subprocessor attachment that we can keep updated.
- Section 4.1 (transfer mechanisms): the current draft references SCCs but doesn't state fallback order when SCCs are not sufficient. Recommend we add an explicit policy: 1) SCCs, 2) EU approved DPF where customer opts in, 3) encryption + contractual safeguards for edge cases.
- Logs/retention: they asked for operational logs — we should confirm which log types we can share (audit trail, request metadata). Suggest we provide examples not PII.

Also flagging that if GlobalHealth wants a DPF-specific attestation, that will require cross-group sign-off (privacy + infra). Karthik — can security provide an excerpt describing network isolation and key custody for Private deployments?

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal & Policy, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-13T11:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for transfer evidence & runbook for DPF review

Thanks Marissa — quick responses below.

- Subprocessors: we maintain a dynamic registry; I can extract the list of infra subprocessors and the region mapping for the next pack. Recommend we include a timestamped manifest PDF (we already do this for SOC2 customers).
- Fallback order: agree with the proposed explicit policy. Operationally we route by customer policy: if customer pinning is set -> route to pinned region; if not pinned -> use cost/latency policy that still respects legal constraints; fallback to compatible model variant in a permitted region if capacity constrained. I'll draft a short paragraph for the runbook.
- Logs: we can produce anonymized request-metadata logs (timestamps, model id, region, token counts). We cannot share raw prompt content unless redacted by the customer.
- Key custody & network: for Private deployments, keys are customer-managed (KMS/HSM) and never leave customer control. For Redwood-hosted: keys are in our KMS with envelope encryption; we can provide KMS configuration and HSM attestation excerpts under NDA. Network map: we'll provide an abstracted diagram showing processing zones and ingress/egress points; no public IP addresses.

I'll prepare the manifest + infra excerpt and send back a proposed language block for the DPA annex by EOD Friday.

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Security Engineering
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@globalhealthsys.com>, procure-ops@globalhealthsys.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Anna Müller <a.mueller@compliance-audit.de>
Date: 2028-06-15T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Request for transfer evidence & runbook for DPF review — supplemental materials

Liam / Anna — attaching the supplemental items Marissa and Karthik prepared: a timestamped subprocessor manifest (pdf), an infra excerpt that explains key custody and network isolation for Private vs Hosted deployments, and a short paragraph we added to Section 4.1 of the DPA annex about fallback order for transfers.

Summary of what's new:
- Subprocessor manifest (timestamped): lists cloud providers, managed DB, logging provider and region mapping.
- DPA annex update: explicit fallback policy added (SCCs -> DPF opt-in -> encryption + contractual safeguards).
- Infra excerpt: how keys are handled and what we can provide under NDA (HSM attestation, KMS configs).
- Example anonymized request metadata sample included (CSV) — note: we are not sending any prompt content.

If Anna's team wants a redline version of the DPA annex or additional attestations, please say which items are priority and we'll route to privacy and infra for sign-off.

Next steps we propose: 1) Anna to confirm whether the manifest and infra excerpt are sufficient for the DPF initial review; 2) Schedule 30-minute walkthrough if helpful; 3) If final DPA changes are requested, we can prepare a redline for signature.

Best,
Vanessa

Attachment(s): subprocessor-manifest-20280615.pdf, infra-excerpt-kms-hsm.pdf, dpa-annex-draft-redline.docx, anonymized-request-sample.csv
From: Anna Müller <a.mueller@compliance-audit.de>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@globalhealthsys.com>, procure-ops@globalhealthsys.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request for transfer evidence & runbook for DPF review — supplemental materials

Thanks Vanessa — received and started review. A few clarifying Qs after a first pass: 

1) The subprocessor manifest is good; can you add the contractual start dates for the listed subprocessors (we need to map effective dates for downstream contracts)?
2) For the infra excerpt: can you provide the specific KMS integration patterns supported (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and whether remote HSM integration (PKCS#11) is supported for Private deployments?
3) The fallback paragraph is helpful — we'll need a short diagram or sequence flow showing decision points (policy match -> region pin -> fallback).

If you can reply with those three items in the next 72 hours we'll be able to proceed to the next stage of the DPF intake.

Anna

--
Anna Müller
Senior Reviewer — Data Protection Frameworks
Compliance Audit (independent reviewer for GlobalHealth Systems)
a.mueller@compliance-audit.de
